findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider rather than an actual BouncyCastle provider; callers relying on BC get the wrong provider or null-like behavior

[Medium/bug] CryptoIntegration.java:detectProvider silently downgrades the previous hard failure on multiple providers to a debug log, hiding classpath misconfigurations and changing runtime provider selection with only debug-level trace

[Low/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:concatenatedRSToASN1DER has two orphaned ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements before the real return value — dead code that is executed and discards output

[Medium/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:asn1derToConcatenatedRS / integerToBytes silently truncates leading significant bytes when toByteArray() is longer than qLength by more than one byte instead of throwing IOException; negative BigIntegers are not rejected
[Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:readSequence does not reject BER indefinite-length encoding; readLength() returning -1 causes the while (length > 0) loop to silently return an empty/partial list

[Low/data] ASN1Decoder.java:readLength uses limit (total stream length) instead of remaining bytes at the current parse position, allowing nested elements to exceed parent bounds and readSequence's length -= bytes.length to underflow silently

[Low/api] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:getKeyStore uses KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()) without a provider, which may resolve inconsistently; consider passing the provider from getBouncyCastleProvider()

[Medium/concurrency] AuthzClient.java:create invokes CryptoIntegration.init(...) on every call; repeated init from multiple threads can race and re-detect/replace the static global provider with no initialize-once guard

[Low/api] AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws bare UnsupportedOperationException in most interface methods; if it wins provider selection (standalone jar), operations like getSignature and getAesCbcCipher fail late at runtime — document which operations are supported

[Low/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java lacks negative tests: malformed DER input (truncated sequence, wrong tag, wrong element count, negative INTEGER), wrong signLength, and cross-check that concatenatedRSToASN1DER output matches JDK/BC-produced DER

[Low/doc_defect] CryptoProvider.java:order() javadoc should state expected tie-breaking behavior (ServiceLoader order), since equal order() values (all three providers return 200) make selection nondeterministic across environments

[Low/bug] ASN1Encoder.java:write(BigInteger) uses signed toByteArray(); a negative BigInteger produces DER that the paired decoder reads back as negative — should validate signum() >= 0 or use unsigned encoding

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CryptoIntegration.java:detectProvider silently downgrades the previous hard failure on multiple providers to a debug log, hiding classpath misconfigurations and changing runtime provider selection with only debug-level trace

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` from throwing on `foundProviders.size() > 1` to instead sorting by `CryptoProvider::order` (descending), selecting `foundProviders.get(0)`, and only logging the remaining providers at DEBUG (`"Ignored crypto providers"`). This does reduce visibility of classpath misconfiguration and changes runtime selection behavior without failing fast, but it appears to be an intentional design change enabled by the newly added `CryptoProvider.order()` method (implemented as `200` in existing providers). So it’s a legitimate review concern about diagnosability/operational safety, not a verifiable correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:concatenatedRSToASN1DER has two orphaned ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements before the real return value — dead code that is executed and discards output
matched_golden_ids: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags dead/orphaned ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements whose output is discarded before the actual return encoding, matching the golden issue of redundant ASN1Encoder operations made irrelevant by a subsequent new encoder in the return statement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:asn1derToConcatenatedRS / integerToBytes silently truncates leading significant bytes when toByteArray() is longer than qLength by more than one byte instead of throwing IOException; negative BigIntegers are not rejected

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider’s ECDSACryptoProvider, asn1derToConcatenatedRS() parses r/s via ASN1Decoder.readInteger() which constructs BigInteger directly from the DER INTEGER bytes (signed), and integerToBytes() then silently truncates whenever s.toByteArray().length > qLength by taking the last qLength bytes. There is no check that the extra leading bytes are only a single 0x00 sign byte (or otherwise safe), and no rejection of negative BigIntegers for r/s. This can accept malformed/malicious DER values and produce incorrect concatenated R/S output without error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:readSequence does not reject BER indefinite-length encoding; readLength() returning -1 causes the while (length > 0) loop to silently return an empty/partial list
matched_golden_ids: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe improper handling of BER indefinite-length encoding where readLength() returns -1. The golden notes that subsequent arithmetic/decrement on a -1 length misbehaves; the candidate notes that using -1 in the loop condition (length > 0) causes incorrect/partial decoding. Same underlying issue: -1 length is not properly handled/rejected, leading to wrong processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] ASN1Decoder.java:readLength uses limit (total stream length) instead of remaining bytes at the current parse position, allowing nested elements to exceed parent bounds and readSequence's length -= bytes.length to underflow silently

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the bounds check for long-form lengths uses the fixed field `limit = bytes.length` (total input size) rather than bytes remaining from the current position (or remaining within a parent element’s declared length). This means an inner element length can exceed the parent SEQUENCE content length yet still be accepted as long as it is < `limit`. Then readSequence() decrements `length` by `bytes.length` without validating it stays non-negative, so an oversized child can make `length` negative and the loop stops silently, having read past the parent’s bounds. This is directly verifiable from the added ASN1Decoder code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:getKeyStore uses KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()) without a provider, which may resolve inconsistently; consider passing the provider from getBouncyCastleProvider()

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getKeyStore(KeystoreFormat format)` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(format.name())` without specifying a provider. The diff also shows other `CryptoProvider` implementations (e.g., `FIPS1402Provider`) explicitly bind keystore creation to a specific provider. While this isn’t a clearly verifiable runtime bug from the diff alone, it is a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency that could matter in environments where the desired keystore implementation depends on a particular provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] AuthzClient.java:create invokes CryptoIntegration.init(...) on every call; repeated init from multiple threads can race and re-detect/replace the static global provider with no initialize-once guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` to `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`, meaning every `AuthzClient` construction triggers a global crypto integration initialization/detection step. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable whether `CryptoIntegration.init(...)` is idempotent or guarded against repeated/concurrent invocation, so the specific claim that it can “race and re-detect/replace” the static provider cannot be confirmed. However, calling a global init on every factory call is a concrete, diff-grounded design/performance/concurrency concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws bare UnsupportedOperationException in most interface methods; if it wins provider selection (standalone jar), operations like getSignature and getAesCbcCipher fail late at runtime — document which operations are supported

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` as a `CryptoProvider` via SPI (`META-INF/services/...CryptoProvider`) and makes `AuthzClient.create(...)` call `CryptoIntegration.init(...)`. In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, most `CryptoProvider` methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `getSignature`, `getAesCbcCipher`, `getAesGcmCipher`, etc.), while only `getEcdsaCryptoProvider()` and `getKeyStore(...)` are implemented. Although `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` now prefers higher `order()` (and authz-client’s provider has `order()` 100 vs other providers’ 200), in a standalone authz-client classpath where this is the only provider it will be selected and any call to unsupported operations would fail at runtime. The diff doesn’t prove those unsupported methods are invoked, so it’s not a confirmed defect, but it is a concrete design/documentation concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java lacks negative tests: malformed DER input (truncated sequence, wrong tag, wrong element count, negative INTEGER), wrong signLength, and cross-check that concatenatedRSToASN1DER output matches JDK/BC-produced DER

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial ASN.1/DER parsing/encoding logic (ASN1Decoder/ASN1Encoder) and ECDSA RS<->DER conversions in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider(). The new ECDSAAlgorithmTest only validates a positive round-trip (DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS) and does not cover malformed DER inputs, wrong element count/tag, negative/odd INTEGER encodings, or invalid signLength values, nor does it assert interoperability by comparing concatenatedRSToASN1DER output to JDK-produced DER. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] CryptoProvider.java:order() javadoc should state expected tie-breaking behavior (ServiceLoader order), since equal order() values (all three providers return 200) make selection nondeterministic across environments

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes provider selection to `sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed())` and then picks `foundProviders.get(0)` without resolving ties. At the same time, three providers in the diff (`DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`) all implement `order()` returning 200, so if more than one is present, selection among equal-order providers depends on ServiceLoader/encounter order, which is not specified here. The finding’s request to document tie-breaking is a valid, diff-grounded review concern, but it’s primarily about clarifying behavior rather than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] ASN1Encoder.java:write(BigInteger) uses signed toByteArray(); a negative BigInteger produces DER that the paired decoder reads back as negative — should validate signum() >= 0 or use unsigned encoding

adjudication.rationale: ASN1Encoder.write(BigInteger) using BigInteger.toByteArray() is the standard DER INTEGER (two’s-complement signed) encoding, and the paired decoder (new BigInteger(bytes)) correctly round-trips that representation. In the only shown usage (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER), r/s are constructed with a leading 0 byte (len+1 array, copy into offset 1), ensuring non-negative values, so the claimed negative-value bug is not introduced/exposed by this diff.
